| **51.4.7** | [ADDED] Verify that confidential client is authenticated for client-to-authorized server backchannel requests such as token requests, pushed authorization requests (PAR), token revocation requests, and token introspection requests. | 2 |

Making this one L2 is quite weird. If we don't authenticate the confidential client for token request, there is not much much reason to make the client confidential in the first place (the client is not acting as a confidential client) 😄

Related to PR #2648

comments.body: The reason for L2 is that it is not a first layer of defense.

We can define the L1 as "if this is the only problem in the application, do you have a (in practice usable) vulnerability".

If there is no authentication for the OAuth client, you can "just" downgrade the confidential client to public client, but it does not provide any immediate attack vector just because of that. It is a second layer of defense.

For reasons above, I close this issue. Note that the requirement content itself is under discussion in #2675
